text: Write three sentences about your favourite meal using only smells and sounds — no taste words allowed.
Describe the school playground using two things you can hear, two you can see, and one you can feel.
Take off your shoes and describe what the grass feels like beneath your feet.
It is early morning in your bedroom. Describe the room using only what you can hear.
A mysterious box is sitting on the desk. Describe it so clearly that a friend could draw it without seeing.
Write about the walk home from school using only colours.
Describe the feeling of climbing into bed on a cold night — two sentences, and neither 'cold' nor 'warm' may appear.
A stranger walks past you in the street. Describe them using exactly one smell and one sound.
Retell your morning from the point of view of the school bell.
Write a complaint letter from a sock that has lost its partner.
Describe your classroom as if you are seeing it for the very first time, from the doorway.
You are the last leaf still holding on to the tree. Write about letting go.
Tell a small story from the point of view of a pencil sitting in a jar.
Your shoes have had a very hard day. Let them speak for themselves.
Write about the sea from the perspective of a stone resting at the bottom.
The old house at the end of the road has watched a hundred families come and go. What does it remember?
Write about an empty playground at night. Nothing bad happens — only mood.
A storm is coming, but nobody else has noticed yet. Build the tension slowly.
Describe a library in the exact moment just before the lights go out.
The first snow of the year falls on your street. Slow everything down.
Write three sentences that make an ordinary kitchen feel unsettling.
It is the last afternoon of the holidays. Capture exactly how that feels.
A single lamp is on in the whole house. Write the scene around it.
Describe a busy train station so that it feels calm rather than noisy.
